When someone calls an airline, texts a retailer, or opens their bank's app and talks to a Sierra agent, our systems carry that conversation.
Phone calls, SMS, WhatsApp, email, and the chat inside our customers' apps all run through this team.
AI voice, chat, and messaging agents are new and they must operate with global communication networks.
Nobody has fully solved how to make the two work together at the speed of a real conversation.
We have to solve it for millions of calls, and you will be building the future of how entire industries will operate with AI agents.
Demo: Finding the perfect stay
Demo: Flight disruption recovery
- Multi-modal: Make one conversation work across voice, text, and screen.
A customer can start by talking, switch to typing on a crowded train, send a photo of a broken part, and get a link or a form back on screen.
The agent remembers everything, whichever way the customer talks and personalizes it.
You will build on the frontier here, and decide what it should feel like.
- Make AI voice feel like a real conversation.
Every call crosses carriers, telephony networks, and contact centers around the world before it reaches our agent.
Making AI agents feel lively and real across global infrastructure is a critical problem to get right for end users.
- Give personal AI agents a safe way in.
More people now have their own AI assistants.
Today a company can either block them or hand them the user's full account access.
The Personal Agent Protocol is an open standard that offers a better option: a safe way for personal agents to work with a company and its Sierra agent.
You'll help build it.
- Build the agent experience inside the app.
ChatKit is our library of native iOS, Android, and web components for talking to an agent.
It covers voice controls, live waveforms, transcripts, and chat.
Customers use it to build an agent experience inside a customer's flagship app, not like a widget added on top.
You decide what those components are and how they behave.
- Get every call to the right agent.
You'll build and own our global telephony stack: SIP, WebRTC, the Sierra Voice Protocol and our integrations with major contact-center platforms.
That means millions of calls and messages, and every one of them reaching the right agent.

You move fast, and you finish what you start.

You go deep where other engineers avoid going: protocols, edge cases, and end to end multi-modal experiences.
- An AI-native way of building.
You not only use AI tools every day, it is ingrained in the way you operate and think.
You've deleted all old priors and re-invented the way you and your teams work from the ground up.
Come ready to tell us about something you built that you couldn't have built 6 months ago.
- An obsession with the details.
When one call in ten thousand fails, you want to know why.
You obsess about the product experience and pixels as much as you do latency and reliability.

The agent must collect and use a card number but can never see it.
This work sits across four hard technical domains: payments, security, real-time voice, and LLMs.
Voice is the core challenge.
A caller speaks or types a card number in a live, low-latency audio stream, and the digits must never reach the model, while the model stays on the call.
Sierra owns every system that touches card data, and one small team owns it end to end across three workstreams: Platform, Product, and Safety & Integrity.
Customers keep their own telephony and payment gateways.
Payments is live in production for some of the largest consumer enterprises, on a platform that handles hundreds of millions of calls a year.
The platform is certified to PCI DSS Level 1.
- Build real-time card capture for voice: intercept keypad and spoken digits in a live audio stream, upstream of the agent runtime in a network-segmented environment, while the LLM stays live on the call.
Make it work across every telephony provider and protocol Sierra supports.
- Build and extend the tokenization platform: agents receive and send short-lived tokens, and the platform swaps a token for the real value only when it calls the customer's payment gateway.
- Own the payments egress control plane: every destination for card data is approved, versioned with the agent release, and enforced by infrastructure below the application, not by convention.
- Make payment actions correct: an at-most-once action primitive in the Agent SDK, validated amounts and items, and monitoring that compares what the agent said about a payment with what really happened.
- Keep card data out of places it should not be: deterministic detection in the agent's hot path that catches what general-purpose models miss.
No LLM, including any we build ourselves, ever sees a plaintext card number.
- Make payments self-serve: one payments API across Agent Studio, the Agent SDK, and Ghostwriter, Sierra's agent-building agent; gateway middleware that developers write against tokens; and support for single-tenant and customer-cloud deployments.
Any team can add payments to an agent without a payments engineer in the loop.
- Grow the platform beyond cards: extend tokenization into a privacy vault for all PII.
WHAT YOU'LL BRING
- 5+ years building backend, platform, or infrastructure systems, with a track record of shipping and operating high-reliability services in production.
- A deep security instinct.
You design as though every component will eventually be compromised, and you reason naturally about blast radius, least privilege, and making bad states impossible rather than reacting to them.
- Rigor about correctness under failure: retries, idempotency, at-most-once behavior, and clear handling of timeouts and unclear results from external systems.
- Fluency in a systems language (we use Go) and comfort owning critical systems end to end, from design through production and on-call.
- Range and ownership.
You like a small team with broad scope, you build clean abstractions over messy external systems, and you're never satisfied solving a problem once per customer.
- Clear communication.
You can explain a design or a risk to other engineering teams and to non-engineers.
- Degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
You don't need payments experience.
The engineers who built this platform came from backend, infrastructure, and security work, not payments.
We care more about how you build correct, secure systems than about the word "payments" on your resume.
EVEN BETTER...
- Real-time or streaming systems: voice, telephony, media, or low-latency pipelines.
- Applied cryptography and key management, network isolation, egress control, or cloud security.
- Platforms other engineering teams build on, such as APIs, SDKs, and self-serve developer services.
- Deployments into customer-owned clouds or single-tenant environments.
- Customer-facing technical work, such as architecture reviews with customers.
- Setting technical direction on ambiguous, high-stakes problems.
- Payments, fintech, or another sensitive-data domain such as healthcare or identity.

Working alongside Agent Engineers, Deployed Infrastructure Engineers, and Agent Strategists, you'll own the programs & strategy that take customers from deployment planning to agents live in production, and continue to support the upgrades and expansion that follow.
You'll bring your technical program management expertise to enterprise AI while establishing the playbooks and ways of working that help this new function scale.
- Own the end-to-end program plan for a customer's in-VPC (Bring Your Own Cloud, BYOC) deployment.
Translate customer requirements into a clear deployment plan, with clear workstreams, owners, milestones, and dependencies across Sierra and customer teams.
- Keep the customer's teams (platform engineering, cloud provisioning, security, networking, model access) aligned and moving, and clear blockers before they hit the launch date.
- Be the translation layer between our engineers and the customer's: define requirements such as model access, observability, and upgrade cadence, and turn technical discussions into actionable next steps.
- Run the operating cadence (standups, weekly status, escalations) so leadership and working groups on both sides always know where the project stands.
- Partner with Sierra's Platform and Deployed Infrastructure teams to feed customer-specific learnings back into our standard deployment offering, runbooks, and tooling, making each subsequent launch more predictable and repeatable.
- Define the TPM function at Sierra as we scale & establish the playbooks, operating rhythms, and standards that future TPMs and customer teams will build on.
WHAT YOU'LL BRING
- 4+ years in technical program management, infrastructure or platform program management, deployment or solutions engineering, or a similar role where you were accountable for delivering complex technical projects across multiple teams.
- A track record of bringing structure to complex technical programs, with strong attention to detail and the follow-through to turn plans into results.
- A strong technical foundation from infrastructure, platform, or complex backend programs.
You can work through technical dependencies with engineers, understand how requirements such as networking, permissions, and provisioning affect delivery, and translate those discussions into a clear plan.
You'll deepen your knowledge of Sierra's architecture and customer deployment environments as you ramp.
- Technical curiosity: you learn new systems quickly, ask thoughtful questions, build context, and apply what you learn to move programs forward.
- Comfort operating inside large, complex enterprise organizations (change management, security reviews, ownership spread across many teams) with the persistence and resourcefulness to keep teams aligned and deployments moving.
- Clear, structured communication: you make complex technical topics, program status, and decisions understandable to engineers and leaders, and adapt your approach to your audience.
- Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
EVEN BETTER...
- Hands-on engineering background (software, DevOps, SRE, or infrastructure) before moving into program or product management, or direct experience with AWS, VPCs, IAM, Kubernetes, or Terraform.
- Experience deploying software into customer-owned cloud environments (BYOC, VPC, or air-gapped), especially at banks or other regulated institutions.
- Familiarity with LLM infrastructure: model gateways, Bedrock or Azure OpenAI, observability for AI systems.
- Experience at an early-stage company where you built the program-management function from scratch.

- Build agents that replace lengthy paper intake forms with conversational experiences, boosting pre-visit intake conversion rates;
- Develop AI agents for healthcare financial platforms that help patients understand billing, payment status, explanations of benefits, and financial assistance eligibility - all while maintaining HIPAA compliance and strong PHI/data privacy safeguards.
